findings.statement: The two round-3 frozen manifests do not replay 7/7 in the delivered working tree: all six gates named by the manifests were rewritten in place during round 8, so all seven rows are could-not-evaluate (gate_digest_mismatch) and tools/replay-frozen.py exits 2. The frozen verdicts themselves are intact: a pristine extraction of the committed revision replays both manifests 7/7, and the repaired gates still reproduce all 7 recorded verdicts byte-for-byte on the frozen inputs (see repaired_gate_behavior_probe). The orchestrator decides between re-freezing the manifest pins, reverting, or quarantining the in-place repairs.

The drift onset is timestamped: both manifests replayed 7/7 with exit 0 at ~20:13Z, and the same commands returned 6/7 with exit 2 at 20:16:12Z after tools/gates/phonology-sanity-gate.py was rewritten (mtime 2026-10-17T20:13:42Z). Verbatim captures: /var/tmp/r8-o16/round-3-replay-pre-repair.txt sha256 f027bb7b64248ccbf0bd537626b480794f7f6a706e624ee86575d80a4a1d3ebf (7/7, exit 0) and /var/tmp/r8-o16/round-3-replay.txt sha256 a6e704651ee9fc3117985ebb4dbe169cfd2539785493f9bad8ad0b6a405c4826 (1 could-not-evaluate, 6 reproduced, exit 2). Both are scratch captures outside the lane; the same 7/7 is reproducible in-lane via the pristine-extraction section of this receipt.

/tmp inode space is exhausted on this host during the 64-worker wave (df -i /tmp: 1048576/1048576 used, 0 free at 2026-10-17T20:16Z); new file creation under /tmp fails with ENOSPC. This is not merely a worker nuisance: tools/replay-frozen.py builds its run mirror under /tmp, so a manifest replay that must actually launch a gate crashes with an unhandled OSError (reproduced traceback under environment.reproduced_failure) while the digest-only rows still report. The final re-run sets TMPDIR to /var/tmp/r8-o16/tmp; the round-8 acceptance harness and the legacy gate selftests were exercised under that TMPDIR. Other workers using the default TMPDIR may be silently failing; the orchestrator should re-run the harness after /tmp is cleared to confirm no artifact depends on this workaround.

Acceptance verdicts at re-run time (delivered tree, TMPDIR set): exit 1, F=true, O=true, D=false. The harness's own failure list at this instant names the remaining D gaps (see validation_rerun.per_claim_after_rerun). The verdicts are a point-in-time measurement of a tree that was still being written (188 dirty paths at run time); they are recorded, not endorsed.
